newsitem.title: USA: Nordstrom reports higher first-quarter profit.
newsitem.headline: Nordstrom reports higher first-quarter profit.

text.p: Nordstrom Inc. on Monday reported better-than-expected first-quarter profits, while May Department Stores Co. and Mercantile Stores Co. Inc. reported lackluster results.
Nordstrom said the stronger quarter reflected higher sales and better cost controls.

The upscale retailer earned a profit of $32.3 million, or 41 cents a share, in the three months ended April 30, a 25 percent rise from $25.9 million, or 32 cents, a year ago. Net sales grew 5.3 percent to $953.7 million from $906 million.
According to First Call, which tracks Wall Street earnings predictions, analysts had expected the company to report a profit of 34 cents a share.
Nordstrom Chairman John Whitacre attributed the improvement to improved cost controls.

"While we have seen a modest rise in sales trends, we are encouraged by improvement in expense control and gross margins that contributed to increased earnings," he said. "We are beginning to see better results in several of our women's apparel departments.
St. Louis-based May Department Stores Co. reported lower first quarter earnings and outlined plans to open new stores during the rest of fiscal 1997.
Earnings declined to $94 million, or 37 cents a share, from $109 million, or 41 cents a share a year earlier.
Revenues rose to $2.59 billion from $2.40 billion.

May said it plans to open nine Lord & Taylor stores, one Strawbridge's store, two Foley's units, and three Filene's stores. May operates 366 department stores currently in 30 states and the District of Columbia.
Fairfield, Ohio-Mercantile Stores Co. Inc. said earnings rose in the quarter but called them "less than satisfactory" because of weak results at new stores.
The company earned $19.3 million, or 52 cents a share, in its first quarter ended on May 3, compared with $13.3 million, or 36 cents per share, a year earlier.

Overall revenues rose to $683.3 million from $655.4 million a year earlier. However, sales in stores open at least one year, known as same-store sales, rose only 1.3 percent in the quarter, compared with a 6 percent rise the year earlier.
Disappointing same-store sales were a "negative contributor to this earnings report which we consider less than satisfactory," Chairman David Nichols said.

The retailer opened five new stores in the fourth quarter of 1996. Since most newly opened department stores operate in the red for the first year, the five outlets were a drag on first-quarter results, Mercantile said.
Mercantile operates 102 department stores under the names McAlpins, Gayfers, Castner Knott and others.
